question.text: An investor bought mutual fund units at NAV of Rs. 15 and redeemed after 540 days at NAV of Rs. 21. Assuming a non-leap year (365 days), the CAGR is closest to:

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook (page 38) applies CAGR over fractional periods using days/365. CAGR = (End/Begin)^(365/days) - 1 = (21/15)^(365/540) - 1 = (1.4)^(0.6759) - 1 ≈ 0.2554, i.e., about 25.5%. The closest listed option is 25.10%. The Trap: Quoting (21-15)/15 = 40% as the return ignores the fractional-period annualisation. Picking 26.72% requires reading the exponent or the ratio incorrectly — the workbook's days/365 method anchors the answer near 25%. Note: For holding periods that are not whole years, always annualise with the days/365 exponent before comparing to other return measures.
